archive.desc: All the schedules computed for this project, starting from the most recent. Name the good ones, group them (by month, by experiment…) and delete the attempts you no longer need. To compute a new one, go to the step

catalog.desc: All the available rules: search by keyword or filter by family. This page is for browsing: to use a rule, go to step 4 ("Rules") and add it to your project, setting its values. Each rule starts out as a requirement or a preference, but you can always change it.
catalog.empty: No rule matches this search. Try another word ("shift", "person", "maximum"…) or remove the filters. If the rule you need is missing, that's a sign it should be added to the catalogue.
catalog.nature_title: Default nature: you can change it when you add the rule
catalog.title: Rule catalogue
composer.empty: No rules yet. Start from the catalogue on the right: for work shifts you almost always need "One shift per day per person" and a "Minimum coverage".
composer.explain_hard: Requirement: if the mandatory rules are incompatible with each other, the engine will find no schedule and will tell you which ones conflict.
composer.explain_soft: Preference: the engine tries to honour it, but may violate it if necessary. The weight decides how much each violation costs.
composer.hint_hard_text: : a non-negotiable rule (e.g. minimum rest required by law). Too many conflicting mandatory rules = no solution.
composer.hint_soft_text: : nice to have (e.g. fairness of night shifts). The engine violates it only when needed, paying the weight you chose.
composer.label_hint: A name of your own to recognise it, e.g. 'At least one senior at night'.
composer.no_results: No rule found: try another word.

composer.toggle_title: A disabled rule stays saved but the engine ignores it
composer.weight_hint: Higher = more costly to violate. Use different weights to say what matters most.
composer.weight_title: How much violating this preference costs: the higher it is, the later the engine sacrifices it
embed.generate_hint: Creates a public link: anyone with the code will see this grid (names included), inside any web page.

people.empty: No people yet. Use the form on the side: type the names, one per line, and press "Add".
people.footer_note: You can always come back here to add or edit people.

profile.delete_text: For now, write to us: deletion permanently removes your projects, schedules and published recipes, so we prefer a human step. Self-service deletion will come with the advanced settings.
profile.email_hint: Service messages and password recovery emails arrive here.
profile.google_hint: You signed in with Google: by setting a password you'll also be able to sign in with your username and password.

project.desc: A project gathers everything a schedule needs: the people to assign, the shifts to cover and the rules to respect. Example: "Cardiology ward — July".
project.desc_placeholder: E.g. 9 nurses, M/P/N shifts, minimum coverage 2
project.how_intro: You work in five steps, following the path in the side menu:
project.how_outro: You can return to any step at any time: your data stays saved on the server.
project.how_step1: Project — you create a container for the schedule.
project.how_step2: People — you add who can work and their skills.
project.how_step3: Shifts — you define the shifts to cover (e.g. morning/afternoon/night for two weeks).
project.how_step4: Rules — you pick constraints from the catalogue: minimum coverage, rest periods, fairness, unavailability…
project.how_step5: Plan — the engine computes the shift table that respects the rules.
project.name_hint: A title you'll recognise: ward, period, room…
project.title: Choose or create a project
run.empty_explanation: The computation succeeded, but no active rule requires assigning anyone: the empty grid satisfies all the requirements (capacity rules only set a ceiling, not a minimum). Add a "minimum coverage" rule to fill the grid.
run.infeasible_help: To unblock: turn one of them into a preference, relax its values, or add people or shifts.
run.infeasible_intro: These requirements cannot all hold at the same time:
run.penalty_title: Sum of the weights of the violated preferences: the lower, the better
run.title: Schedule #{id}

runs.missing_slots: there are no shifts to cover (step 3)
runs.no_rules: No active rules: the result will be an arbitrary grid.
runs.step_desc: The engine tries every person–shift combination and returns the table that satisfies the requirements while violating preferences as little as possible. Here you see the most recent computations; the full history, with names and groups, is in the "Schedules" section.
runs.time_limit_title: Maximum time granted to the engine. If it runs out, it keeps the best solution found so far.
slots.desc: A shift is a box to fill: a day plus a time band (e.g. "Monday 7 July, Morning"). Instead of entering them by hand, describe the day's bands and the period: we generate them for every day.
slots.empty: No shifts yet. Set the bands and period in the form on the side and press "Generate": we'll create one shift for each day × band.
slots.footer_note: Hover over a shift with the mouse to delete it individually.
slots.hint_1: The band code is free-form: instead of M/P/N you can use
slots.hint_2: … Each day + code combination is a box the engine can assign to a person.
slots.hint_title: What if my 'shifts' are rooms or workstations?
slots.step_bands: 1 · The time bands of the day
slots.title: Define the shifts to cover

store.desc: Tried-and-tested rule sets published by the community: install one into your project and adapt the values instead of starting from scratch. When your rules work well, give back: publish them here.
store.description_placeholder: Who is it for? What problems does it solve? What needs adapting?
store.empty: The store is still empty. Got a rule set that works? Be the first to publish it.
store.field_description: Description — help others understand when to use it
store.hint_p1_2: (type, parameters, requirement/preference, weights): never people, shifts or data from the original project. Rules tied to specific people (unavailability, pairs…) are excluded automatically at publication.
